terms.definition: An installable unit with a plugin.json: its pages, sections, settings and declarations.
A function that core defines and several plugins can serve; a plugin lists its categories in categories and the categories it needs in requires.
The tab of the main window that shows the settings of the application and of its plugins, beside the project tabs.
The launcher of a window without an open project: a search, the pinned and recent projects, and the buttons to create or open one.
A native program of one domain with a sidecar.json that plugin pages talk to.

A repository whose release is a tool that several repositories run in their checks or releases, a build input of those repositories. The application never installs it, and it is not a layer of the application.

The file that a registry lists: the pnpm pack file of a plugin, <scope>-<name>-<version>.tgz, the npm pack file of a sidecar, <file name>-<version>-<platform>.tgz, or soksak-<version>-<platform>-<host>.zip of an application bundle.
The folder that plugins/installed.json records for an installed plugin.
A document of a plugin that a document region shows at soksak://<plugin id>/<path>.
A native region of a surface that shows the transfer images of a sidecar (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md).
The acknowledged removal of one image generation's render ownership and configuration while retaining its surface session (docs/spec/sidecars.md#image-envelope).
An address soksak://<owner>/<command> that opens from outside the application.
The file logs/application.log under the configuration directory: the host lines, the page lines sent through report, and the standard error of the sidecars that the host starts.
The events page.trace.*, host.trace.*, host.sampler.* and sidecar trace events that the layers store in the event files under logs/ while the setting diagnostics.performance is on.
A file logs/state-<time>.json that the debug view writes: the state of the host, the versions and every window at one time.
The dialog that Help > Debug opens: it records a state file, lists the files of logs/ and saves them.
One record of the contract in docs/spec/logging.md: a JSON object with a time, a sequence number, a level, a layer, a declared name and fields.
The declared kind of an event (lifecycle, input, call, io, frame) that decides how the writer stores it.

One kind of data of a document region, its elements or its requests: the host collects the element tree only while a page subscribes to the `elements` stream, and the requests of the region from its attach to its close, whatever the subscriptions (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#document-streams).
The elements of a document region at one point, sent as {seq, nodes, total, truncated} under acknowledgement of its seq.
The identifier that one native input receives from the layer that first sees it and that every later layer carries (cids in an event).

The rules by language that list each source of occurrences (an empty catch, a discarded result, a goroutine, a registered observer, an error return) and require an event in its function or a reason marker.
The one comment form (default|silent): <reason> that states why a source of occurrences stores no event.
Rebuilding the screen of a session from its stored inputs with the replay executable of its sidecar, to compare the stored hashes of the screens (docs/spec/replay.md).
The events of the layer sidecar that one run (boot) of a sidecar produced for one session; its sequence restarts at 1, and a replay compares each segment on its own (docs/spec/replay.md#segments).
The SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of a screen, a grid of cells with a cursor, that docs/spec/replay.md defines; a sidecar and a page store it per frame record.
The diagnostic nonce and source generation, raster, and sequence encoded in a visible QR code to correlate a captured image with its exact source raster.
A diagnostic nonce and source generation and sequence encoded in a visible QR code rendered by a plugin view document, used to identify that code in a ScreenCaptureKit WindowServer output sample.

An explicitly started diagnostic fixed overlay with a transparent background and a unique opaque border whose captured pixels identify the visual viewport edges without changing document layout or input.

A provider-defined runtime grid coordinate used to place an input caret in a raster presentation overlay; it is distinct from the engine cursor and is not part of the generic screen hash or replay inputs.
A stored-format change that moves folders or crosses files: it has no definition, its release documents it and reinstalling carries it out.
The kind of a stored file of a configuration folder or a project root: numbered, transient, log, external or fetched.
The core operation of the memory saver that releases the surface of a hidden tab that stays in the layout; the tab keeps its reports and the state its plugin wrote.
The core operation of the memory saver that mounts an unloaded tab again from the state its plugin wrote when the tab is shown.
A reason of the memory saver that keeps a tab from being unloaded, such as shown, keep:modified or media.
The core function, turned on and off by the setting memorySaver, that unloads hidden tabs after a delay and under memory pressure and restores them when they are shown.

A separate web view of a plugin on its soksak://<plugin id> origin, with one view per tab and one per sidebar section, in which the plugin draws its screen by any means (free DOM, a framework or library, text input with an input method, a canvas or editor, or a document region or image region).
The object {sidebar, section, key, path?, role?} that a request uses to address one control of a declared section (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
One sidebar as core.sidebars reports it, identified by left, right, top, bottom, or cardId:side.

The order of the four sides left, right, top and bottom that the setting sidebarOrder holds: the window sidebars take the room of the plane in that order, and the sidebar of the first side that holds one reaches across the whole plane along its side.

A sidebar section whose every element is one of list, tree, button or status-line, which the workbench draws from the declared UI snapshots and pull replies that a plugin sends (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The message that carries one declared UI value of one status, pushed by the plugin with {plugin, status, seq, value, skipped} and acknowledged by seq.
One node of a declared UI value: a list, tree, button or status-line, or an item or node of a list or tree (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The declared element that shows one line of plain text in a declared UI value (docs/spec/declared-ui.md). It is not the status line that ends a window sidebar.
The schema of the value of a declared UI status, which the plugin declares in exposes.status and the receiver validates with the rules of docs/spec/declared-ui.md.
A status that a sidebar section names with the `status` form of its declaration, whose value is a declared UI value (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
A tree node with a nonempty children array or `branch: true`, which the workbench draws with an expand control (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
A tree node with `branch: true` and no child nodes in the current value; it has an expand control while its children are absent (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
A sidebar section declared with the `status` form, whose body the workbench draws from a declared UI status (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The value of a declared UI status: an object with the field `elements` that a declared UI snapshot or pull reply carries (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The response of a pull of a declared UI status: {seq, value}, where value is the source's current value and is null when the source has no value yet (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The pair of a process and its registration of a declared UI status (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).

A plugin's override of the content of a fixed window sidebar, which applies only while the focused card's active surface is that plugin's (docs/spec/external-sidebars.md, Override context and rail border).
The mark of a status whose value changed while its snapshot was in transit; the acknowledgement of that snapshot sends the latest value of the status and clears the mark.
A process of a plugin, with a platform web view attached to the window, that runs DOM-free logic which neither a view nor a sidecar can hold; it exists only when the contract requires it.
A call across a process boundary from its start until it receives its reply or ends with a timeout, a lost peer or a failure; the core status core.plugin.open-calls counts the open calls of a plugin.
The createCalls module of plugin-api that sends a call over a transport, resolves or rejects it by its reply, and reports its timeouts, lost peers, late replies and open calls.
A count of a loss, a skipped value, a late reply or a presentation abandoned, kept in the core status core.plugin.losses per plugin until the application ends; it is not a log event in a release.
The view surface of one sidebar section, with the surface id <space id>/<sidebar id>/<section id>, which the sidebar places in the body of the section (docs/spec/plugins.md#sections).
The wait of a window commit for a view to present its content after a card layout change.
The table that a view registers with its host, holding each workbench shortcut and its owner.
The fields of a call: its id, command and cancellation; a reply carries the same id.
The reserved host `core` on the soksak:// scheme, which serves the view import map targets, the shared modules and the modules of granted items to views, and which no plugin id can use.
The module `@soksak/plugin-api/view` that a view page imports, which exports the view side of the call layer and of the declared UI snapshots over the view channel.

The import map of a view page, with the five entries `soksak`, `@soksak/plugin-api`, `@soksak/plugin-api/view`, `@soksak/plugin-api/screen-hash` and `@soksak/shared/`, which map to their `soksak://core` addresses.

A contribution of a plugin to an extension point of another installed plugin, whose provider is installed and enabled, whose range contains the version of the point, and whose entry matches the schema of the point.
A contribution item whose provider is installed and enabled and whose range contains the version of the point, used only by the core root grant.
The document-start script and the message handler `sok-view` that the host registers with a view's web view configuration, through which a view page sends and receives its calls and snapshots.

The web view configuration that the host creates for one view, with `isView`, the plugin id of the surface, the document-start scripts of the view channel and of the theme, and the handler `sok-view`.
The document of a view whose ready message the host has recorded, the only document that receives host messages.
The file plugins/installed.json, which maps each plugin id to its recorded path.
The key that identifies the owner of an exposure registration.
A session that a surface of a plugin opens with `core.session.open` and that no tab shows until a tab shows it on request (docs/spec/plugins.md#owned-sessions).
The surface that opened an owned session and may resize or end it, whose close ends the session with reason `owner-closed`.
A declared UI snapshot that is sent for one status and not yet acknowledged.
The name field of a plugin's package.json. The installation record does not hold it.

The bytes that a document region keeps for its plugin under binary ids, from an upload until a download or a native take releases each id, or until the region closes (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#document-regions).
The 32-character lowercase hexadecimal id that the host mints for one stored upload of a document region's binary store.
The value that the host page of a plugin saves through its channel and that the host keeps for the next start of the page (docs/spec/plugin-host.md).

The control that keyboard focus moves to for a declared tree node: its label control when that control exists and is enabled, otherwise the expand control of a branch (docs/spec/declared-ui.md, Tree keys).
An independent ordinary AppKit text view in an application window that diagnostic activation checks compare with the same native keys.
The request-local array of declaration objects referenced by surface start values in a native surface synchronization request.
Whether the supplier of an image region draws its raster: the outer surface of the region is visible and its window is on screen, neither occluded nor minimized (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md).

How the host presents the transfer images of an image region, which the region declares as `present`: `copy`, where the host copies each accepted image into host-owned storage and answers `consumed`, or `lease`, where the host presents the supplier's IOSurface itself (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md).

The presentation mode in which the host holds the supplier's IOSurface of an accepted frame and its image layer presents it, answered `leased`, until a later frame replaces it, the region closes or its generation is detached, answered `released` (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md).

The host package of one language that holds every part of a host that names no framework, its bindings, windows, workspace, surfaces, documents, images, sidecars, exposure, endpoint, event log, diagnostics and darwin platform layer among them, and reaches the framework of its application only through the framework port.

The host package of one framework that holds the run of the application, the implementations of the framework port and every file that only that framework needs, and links the language host library of its language.

The two interfaces through which the language host library reaches a framework, named the same in both languages: `Framework`, with the application name, the main-thread step, quit, dialogs, menus, the Dock and window creation with its title bar, and `Frontend`, with the event emit, the window title, show, focus, the window events, the presentation notice, the settled presentation, the workbench start and the workbench call channel.

The workbench that the host draws in native UI with the widgets and layout of its framework instead of a JavaScript page in a web view, so that a window has no main page and the workbench start builds the workbench again instead of reloading a page.

The view that the application places in a window under the surface that the native workbench draws on, filling the content of the window until the window closes, which holds the container of the surface hosts of that window.

An element of the native workbench that names a view inside the native view of the window and the key view of the element, paints a hole over the box of the named view, computes the covers that the workbench draws over it and, in the frame that draws the element, gives its box, clip and covers to the application, which sets the frame of the named view in the same transaction as that frame.

The notice that the frame which drew a given scene of a window has presented, for which the layout transaction waits through the framework port: the presentation update of the main page on a host with a main page, and on the native workbench a callback of the framework that runs once after that frame presents or reports that the scene presented nothing, for want of damage, for want of a drawable or because the window holds its frames.

The block of the framework port that brings the content of a window to the screen in its current state and then calls back, which the settled wait of the surface layout takes in place of the main web view: on a host with a main page the read of its document and its next presentation update, and on the native workbench a frame without a hold that calls back on its presentation notice.

The part of `Frontend` in the framework port through which the language host library delivers a call to the workbench of a window, which a framework adapter of the native workbench passes on through its `Workbench` interface.

The table of the allowed differences between the host packages of the two languages, with the columns Go and Rust, whose rows H name files of the language host libraries, rows C files of the command line packages and rows E endpoint methods that one language does not have, with row IDs unique across it and the framework table.

The table of the allowed differences between the host packages and the applications of the frameworks, with one column per framework, whose rows H name files of the framework adapters, rows A files of the applications and rows B host calls that the workbench of one framework does not make, with row IDs unique across it and the language table.

A host with a main page built from the revision that completes the measurement targets of the three-host benchmark, before any change of the code that such a host runs, which installs the plugin releases recorded for it and against which the benchmark judges the host of the native workbench and finds each regression of the other host of its framework.
A host with a main page built from the same revision as the host of the native workbench, which the three-host benchmark measures in the same session and against which it judges that host.

The tree of the elements of the native workbench of a window with their names, roles, frames and actions, which the framework builds in every build when the host asks for it and from which the binder audit, element rectangles and element actions take their answers.
An exposure entry of the kind `element`, which names an element of the workbench or of a view.
The name of an element entry, by which a window check addresses its element.
A set of two or more touching content cards of one space that is drawn with one outer outline, with an optional leader card.
The one card of a party that carries the leader mark and the leader color, or none if the party has no leader.
A rectangle of the layout of a space, placed by the layout: a content card, which holds one or more tabs, or a window sidebar, which is a fixed card of the plane (docs/spec/external-sidebars.md).
A card of a space whose one or more tabs hold content, as opposed to a window sidebar, which is a fixed card of the plane and holds sections.
One arrangement of the cards of a project, with its focused card, card sidebar widths and tabs, saved in the projects.json of the project (docs/spec/projects.md#persistence).
The role that soksak assigns to a tab of an agent CLI, defined by one agent role definition and read by the agent from its role file (docs/spec/agent-roles.md).
The file `<config-dir>/agents/<surface>/role.md` that holds the text of the agent role of one tab; soksak writes it and the agent reads it (docs/spec/agent-roles.md#role-file).
An injected message of soksak that names the path of a role file and carries no role text, and tells an agent that its role changed (docs/spec/agent-roles.md#change-message).

The text that soksak sends as the first message of each session of an agent CLI. It names the role file of its tab and the rule that messages beginning with the role prefix assign the role (docs/spec/agent-roles.md#stable-identity).
The file that the measured launch of Claude Code read for its stable identity in the measured facts of the agent role contract; no current launch writes it (docs/spec/agent-roles.md#measured-facts).

The first 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters of the SHA-256 digest over a role identifier, a line feed and the stored definition text; it identifies the current role file (docs/spec/agent-roles.md#role-file).
The integer that starts at 1 and rises by one at each change of the agent role or its definition in a tab (docs/spec/agent-roles.md#tab-role-state).

A message that names the role file of a tab and asks its agent to read the file again and confirm its fingerprint. soksak sends one at each not-busy report of the agent CLI while the role is pending, with no limit; the count is the `requests` of the status (docs/spec/agent-roles.md#requests).

The agent's answer that it holds the current fingerprint of its role file, given by `sok role confirm <fingerprint>` or by the line `soksak role <fingerprint>` (docs/spec/agent-roles.md#confirmation).
An injected message of soksak that concerns the agent role of a tab: a change message or a reread request (docs/spec/agent-roles.md#change-message).

The event record that the terminal page writes for each decision on an injected message: `plugin.<plugin>.messages.delivered`, with its kind, sequence, path, sender, state and reason (docs/spec/messaging.md#delivery).
The one display path that shows an error to the person and writes it to the application log at the moment it appears, in the form `error: <where>: <text>`.
A login of a person that a plugin declares with `accounts` in `plugin.json`: the record `{id, name, kind}` in the plugin key `accounts`, whose CLI keeps its login in the home of the account.
The folder `accounts/<id>` of the data folder of a plugin, where the CLI of an account keeps its login and settings.

A record of the notification path of core that the person sees: its kind (success, info, warning, error or progress), title, text, source, actions and time. A notice shows on the status line of its card, as a toast and in the notice center.
The list of every notice of the application, opened by the bell of the title bar as a popover or a drawer; it keeps an error until the person clears it and every other notice for 7 days.
A notice shown under the bell of the title bar for a limited time or until the person closes it, in the form that the setting toastStyle chooses.
A notification that the host posts through the notification center of the operating system for a notice whose plugin sets system.
